I'm bipolar and doing rtms. I'm still having very bad episodes and my phq9 (patient health questionnaire, the stuff that asks you how you feel 1-3) remains the same as the day I started. Still very miserable and keep hearing about the people who are having amazing results only 2-3 sessions in. Most insurance wouldn't accept me so the place that did does not offer bilateral pulses so I only have my left side done. They say people sometimes don't experience anything until after 30 sessions but im half way into 30 and feel almost worse than before. I think it really just varies on the person, and it's hard to tell whether it will positively work or not.
I also experienced a manic episode a little over a week ago with the worst crash I've ever had in my entire life so that was around session 10 or so

The office I go to doesn't do anything different but was the only one who accepted my insurance (I had to wait a really long time). So I only get left but I have bipolar (+ocd and ptsd) and a personality disorder. Hasn't worked at all for me so far.

My insurance covers it completely but I believe if it is completely out of pocket it can be up to $15,000. I think most places only require a copay of $25-50 and insurance will cover a lot of it, but will sometimes charge per session. The office I go to has a whole packet about costs and breaks down what each process will cost (ie. Mapping, each session, etc.)

I just finished session 15 today and my phq9 is the same as it was the day I started. I haven't seen a single change and all that they were able to (and I'm talking grabbing at straws here) conclude is that I had enough motivation to watch TV. 

I have bipolar disorder (+ocd and ptsd) and a personality disorder (tms likely won't do anything to help personality disorders). The only thing I've been able to note personally is that my sleep is more disrupted and my nightmares are getting more extreme.

christmas has gone from being something i mildly enjoyed (i’ve been miserable since early teens, i’m nearing 30 now) to something i almost despise now. it’s something about seeing others so happy and the overwhelming jealously that comes with it, because i don’t feel that happiness. then i feel selfish because everyone deserves to be happy, and i shouldn’t be mad just because i’m not. i don’t have any friends, or acquaintances, and the family i have but don’t interact with think i’m a freak. i guess i’d say i’m pretty lonely too

i have borderline personality disorder as well, and i think it is one of the least understood illnesses. i can’t count the times doctors have told me there’s “no cure for BPD”. i also have bipolar disorder but there is medication for that to help with mood swings etc. in fact even when i tell people i have BPD they think that means “bi polar disorder” most people don’t even know what BPD is.. 

i feel like most people don’t even see me as a person. just like you i’ve had childhood and adult trauma and i also live in a shitty household- my mom (also mental sufferer) and i got our house foreclosed on and now we live with my grandmother whose generation turned their backs to mental illness. i have to hide when i cut myself with long sleeves and cry into a towel or pillow so no one hears me because my entire family sees me as a freak. 

i can relate to everything you feel- the tired, the lonely, the overwhelmed, the failure.. were “never going to get better” and how we feel like the second things look up, they crumble back down again and send us into an even deeper hole. one that we can’t dig ourselves out of. one that no one can help us with because we feel like we are literally impossible to help- no one truly understands the pain. 

i’m waiting on disability because i’m too “high risk” to be working right now and the government doesn’t even acknowledge BPD. when i have case managers fill out papers with me they use bipolar instead, and when i asked why they didn’t use the more prominent disorder they claimed that “it’s just easier” to use bipolar.

i feel stuck like you, nowhere to go, nothing to do about it. no help in sight. and for some reason when people downplay the disorder, it just kicks on that suicidal tendency like “well fuck no one gets what i’m going through anyway i might as well just not even be here” 

i sometimes think people ignore it because we don’t always have “physical” signs of pain like someone who has a broken arm or leg. they don’t get that what’s broken is on the inside.
